newsitem.title: UK: Ladbroke says no plans to take HHC stake.
newsitem.headline: Ladbroke says no plans to take HHC stake.

text.p: Ladbroke chief executive Peter George said on Monday his company had no current plans to take a stake in partner Hilton Hotels Corporation (HHC).
George was speaking at a press conference after Ladbroke and HHC sealed an alliance to reunite the Hilton hotel brand worldwide for the first time in 32 years.
HHC owns the name in the U.S., while Ladbroke's Hilton International subsidiary holds the rights elsewhere.
Under the deal, each company can take a stake of up to 20 percent in the other. HHC intends to take a five percent stake in Ladbroke in due course.

Explaining the decision not to take a stake in HHC, Ladbroke's George said that the company had "a different sort of balance sheet" from HHC. But he added that Ladbroke intended to invest in HHC gaming projects in the future.

George said that it had not yet been settled how HHC would acquire its stake in Ladbroke. He said the shares could be purchased in the market over a period or new shares issued, or a combination of the two.
HHC President and CEO Stephen Bollenbach told the news conference that he did not envisage job losses as a result of the alliance.
"This is really about expanding expanding revenues and not cost-saving," Bollenbach said.
Bollenbach said that the two companies had explored every possible avenue, including merger, during their talks on reuniting the brand.
But he said that all of the benefits the two companies were seeking could be achieved without the larger capital investment and the complications of a merger.
He would not be drawn on the prospects of a merger at some later date, saying the future would look after itself.
